product: KeyLoad development preview. Not production ready.
concept: Orleans owns all clustering and activation scaling. The API reaches one grain per connected client, logical database/partition grains, storage owners and bounded result aggregation. Shared volumes require one open owner per physical partition without copies; isolated volumes use typed Orleans calls between owners. Shared-volume ownership and distributed partition-query execution are not yet qualified.

evidence: Qualification evidence lives only in GitHub Actions runs and their original artifacts for the exact delivered source.
implementation: Orleans-execution runtime integration is in progress. The commit grain caches copy owners per membership version instead of reading every silo per write; the ZoneTree engine runs without its own WAL because commands.wal is the only redo log; the SQL gateway lowers SELECT once to the typed plan and the SDK carries no parser; stateless background workers sweep persisted work with one polling activation per silo and no in-memory buffer; internal grain requests are typed Orleans envelopes validated by scope on every receiving grain, with no per-hop string token or HMAC (ADR-144); a store commit holds the exclusive gate only while applying, so readers no longer wait for the journal fsync; key encoding takes typed components without boxing; the comparison harness has no warm-up phase anywhere. Request handling imposes no concurrency, request-count or reserved-byte admission on callers (ADR-145): the HTTP, command and MCP memory admission pools, the per-connection, per-silo producer and connection caps, the ANN reader caps, the per-engine analytical-read cap, the change-outbox producer quota and progress reserve, and the full-text reader and maintenance-session count caps are gone; only the server-wide request-body limit and the physical reply and protocol bounds remain, and the KeyLoad benchmark cells no longer carry an admission profile. Operations have no configured size or work limits (ADR-149): KeyLoad:DatabaseLimits keeps only the optional queue transfer attempt policies; document size, JSON depth, batch, scan, result, SQL text/depth/token, read-byte, search-token, projection and fixed-deadline refusals are gone; reads account work and stop only on caller cancellation and explicit expiries, complete ranges page through the storage range page, recursive SQL, AST and JSON walkers fail with Validation only when the execution stack runs short, and result bytes are bounded by the grain reply ceilings and the optional QueryExecutionOptions.MaximumResultBytes. Concurrent canonical commands commit in batches (ADR-146): the reentrant commit grain queues them, every copy applies a batch as one ZoneTree commit with one journal flush and parallel copy calls, each command keeps its own canonical sequence and outcome, and a copy that missed the last batch is completed from its retained commands; the engine and store contracts have unit tests, while cluster throughput and fault qualification of the batch path remain open. Queries ordered by ascending document id continue after the last emitted id instead of an offset (ADR-147): a full scan seeks past that id and stops one row past the page, so reading a collection page by page reads each document once, and no query range read asks storage for more than its per-range maximum. Build and Tests runs as parallel jobs (ADR-148): one solution build gate, four unit shards, analyzers with process recovery, and twelve Aspire shards of two serial lanes each with at most one cluster per lane, all from scripts/Features/TestInfrastructure/ci-test-shards.json; a final job checks that every test class ran exactly once, and Release runs this workflow before publishing; each source revision requires its own successful original execution and exact-once verification artifacts. IsolatedVolumes uses silo-local full copies; SharedVolume acquires one physical session through an ordinary database activation and joins its borrowers before close. PartitionQuery and DistributedSearch dispatch bounded leaves through ordinary Orleans partition grains and pin one actual owner per logical partition. Workers and durable coordinators use typed owner reads. Complete runtime and delivered-source qualification is open.
